calls.reason: The packet has only a 2022 OpenAI loss figure, Microsoft's cloud gross margins and one productivity study. Nothing measures industry-wide profit or loss for late 2023, and 'worth' is undefined.

Synergy's 67% share covers all cloud infrastructure, not AI spending. The Anthropic–Google hosting deal shows how money flows but not what share reaches the big firms, so 'almost every dollar' can't be tested.

Before the post, WebArena found GPT-4 finished about 14% of practical web tasks, against 78% for humans. The customer-support gains came from assisting people, not automating their work, which fits the claim of little sign of broad automation.

The evidence is one Coca-Cola ad: online backlash, and a System1 test where most viewers felt positive and few noticed errors. A single campaign doesn't settle how ordinary viewers react to visual glitches, and the claim is framed as opinion.
Developer counts and Anthropic's Claude Pro launch don't show how revenue split between product integrations and direct subscriptions in late 2023. Dependence can't be judged.

Stanford's 2026 AI Index reports models improved rapidly in 2025, with scores rising in language, reasoning, coding and math, and video generation advancing. That is over two years after the post said the top of the S-curve was near.
